quote: So there's gonna be, like, an energy hike with the grid. So we're just kinda trying to be proactive with that and stuff.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong forward-looking anchor — anticipated rate hikes with AEP — that practically hands the rep the alignment-against-utility flip. The rep replies only with agreement, not reinforcement.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer already sold on the concept (he raised the concern unprompted) and saw no need to push further, since the call ended in a booking anyway.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect the customer's own words back as the reason to act now — e.g., tying the appointment to locking in ahead of the hike he mentioned — rather than just validating and moving to the next verify item.

stewart_read: The $200 bill figure is captured cleanly but the rep immediately pivots to the address verification with no acknowledgment of what that number means for the customer or the design.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally deferring bill-pain framing to the closer, since setter scope discipline says not to sell — but bill_anchoring guidance treats capture-and-flip as the setter's job, not the closer's.
coaching_implication: Replay this moment with the rep: after capturing a number, add one line connecting it to the customer's own rate-hike concern before moving to the next verify item.

quote: the main requirements are that you pay income tax and have a credit score above six fifty.
stewart_read: Rep states a 650 threshold where the schema records 670. This is the second call in the corpus where a rep has stated 650, but two instances is not enough to call this a floor-wide pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: The 650 figure could reflect an actual updated Ion policy the schema hasn't caught up to, rather than rep error.
coaching_implication: Worth confirming with Kenny whether 670 or 650 is the current active threshold so reps are consistent; not a call-specific coaching failure on this rep's part.

quote: It was I think it was recently, but I couldn't, like, before we moved in about so I mean, fairly fairly new, but as far as that, I can't I can't give you the next
stewart_read: Customer gives a vague, unconfirmed roof age. Rep accepts "pretty new for a roof" without probing for an actual age or asking if there's documentation, leaving the qualifier soft heading into the closer call.
alternative_hypothesis: Since roof age wasn't a hard DQ trigger here (no stated concern about age over 15 years), rep may have reasonably judged this not worth further digging on a cooperative call already running smoothly.
coaching_implication: Encourage a light follow-up question (e.g., "any idea on the year?") when the customer's answer is this uncertain, so the closer isn't walking in blind on roof condition.

stewart_read: Rep correctly refuses to book a time that excludes the wife, restating "we'd prefer she's there" and offering an evening alternative — textbook protocol adherence rather than treating this as an objection to overcome.
coaching_implication: Positive example to reinforce with this rep: this is the correct move under protocols.spouse_decision and should be recognized as a strength, not just a gap-hunt target.

quote: Yeah. I mean, if something comes up, something comes up, we'll plan on 7PM on Tuesday
stewart_read: The appointment is booked at 7PM Tuesday but the wife's attendance is explicitly left uncertain ("I'm not sure on her schedule") and the rep books anyway without a firm double-confirm.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have pushed for a definite yes/no on her schedule before locking the time. Strategic read: given her unpredictable clinic schedule, locking a placeholder time and letting the closer/text-confirm handle the final check may be the most workable path rather than stalling the booking.
coaching_implication: Flag for the closer: wife's attendance at 7PM Tuesday is not confirmed. Rep should also consider a text reminder specifically asking the wife to confirm ahead of the appointment.

quote: I just wanna make sure she's involved, obviously, when we give the estimate.
stewart_read: Rep proactively states the intent to include the co-owner well before scheduling even comes up, showing awareness of the protocol early rather than reacting to it later.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the correct early flag — naming the intent to include the spouse right at the co-owner verify question, not waiting until scheduling friction forces it.
